title: Sensing of Barrier Tissue Disruption with an Organic Electrochemical Transistor
protocol: Mix ethylene glycol into 50 ml of PEDOT:PSS in a volume ratio of 1:4.
Add 0.5 μl/ml of Dodecylbenzenesulfonic acid (DBSA) as a surfactant to the mixture.
Dissolve 10 mg/ml of 3-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane (GOPS) in the PEDOT:PSS solution as a cross-linker.
Spin coat photoresist on a clean glass slide at 3,000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Define patterns by photolithography.
Develop the patterned photoresist using a developer.
Evaporate 5 nm of chromium and then 100 nm of gold on the substrate with lift-off lithography.
Lift off the photoresist in an acetone bath for 1 hour, leaving only Au contacts on the glass slide.
Load 3.5 g of parylene-C into the coating setup.
Evaporate 2 μm of parylene-C uniformly over the substrate with Au contacts.
Spin coat photoresist at 3,000 rpm for 30 seconds after evaporating parylene-C.
Use a mask to illuminate channel and gold contact areas under UV light for 20 seconds.
Develop the exposed photoresist using a developer to open the channel area.
Etch the Pa-C in the channel area by a 15 min plasma step (O₂ (50 sccm) and CHF₄ (3 sccm) plasma at 160 W).
Deposit the PEDOT:PSS mixture solution by spin coating at 500 rpm for 45 sec.
Bake the sample for 30 sec at 110 °C.
Peel-off the Pa-C to reveal the PEDOT:PSS channel of the substrate underneath.
Bake samples for 1 hr at 140 °C under atmospheric conditions.
Mix two solutions (usually supplied together in a kit) at a ratio 1:10 of curing solution in base solution to make PDMS.
Bake the PDMS for 1 hr at 120 °C.
Design well by using a hole punch and cut a square around the desired area.
Glue a PDMS well on top of the channel, ensuring that the source and drain contacts are not covered.
Make a plastic support with a hole in it (can use the holder for the cell culture insert).
Glue the plastic support on top of the PDMS.
Let the assembly dry overnight.
Test the well for leaking by prefilling with water.
Solder electric wires on the source and drain contact with tin.
Prepare cell culture media as follows: In DMEM, add 1% Glutamine, 10% Fetal Bovine Serum, 0.5% Penicillin-streptomycin, and 0.1% Gentamicin.
Sterilize the cell culture media using a sterile filter device.
Maintain Caco-2 cells between passage 49 and 68 at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO₂.
Maintain the Caco-2 cells in cell culture media.
Divide cells once a week using trypsin.
Seed at 1.5 x 10^4 cells/insert.
Change cell culture media twice a week over 3 weeks.
Connect an Ag/AgCl wire to a sourcemeter for use as the gate electrode.
Immerse the tip in cell culture media, which is used as the electrolyte.
Connect wires from source and drain to the sourcemeter (dual channel setup).
Apply a square pulse positive voltage between the gate and the source (used as reference electrode: ground).
Apply a negative constant voltage between drain and source.
Measure corresponding current.
Use a PC running program for data collection.
Enter OECT parameters in a customized acquisition program: VDS = -0.2 V, VGS = 0.3 V, VGS on time = 2 sec, off time = 28 sec.
Read out source-drain current (IDS) and gate current (IGS).
Carry out the measurement for several minutes to ensure a stable baseline signal.
Prior to the experiment, verify the integrity of the cell layer by measuring TER with an Impedance spectroscopy device.
Ensure TER of each 3-week old Caco-2 cell insert is above 400 Ω.cm^2.
During off time of OECT measurement: Remove the gate electrode from the electrolyte.
Incorporate the cell culture insert.
Replace the gate electrode inside the cell culture insert.
Carry out a baseline measurement with the cells for several minutes to ensure a stable signal.
Prepare a 1 M solution of EGTA in DI water, adjusting the pH to 7.4 with Tris base.
Add EGTA solution in the appropriate volume to obtain the desired concentration between 5 mM and 100 mM.
Add EGTA solution in the basal chamber during the off time.
Measure continuously for 90 min.
At the end of the run, scratch the cell layer to result in a complete destruction of the barrier layer.
Immerse the gate electrode in the media after removing the filter.
Measure for 15 min.
